label: rem:gram-kappa-spectral-interpretation
title: Plancherel form of $\kappa$ replaces the 2-jet hand calculation
html:
Remark. Plancherel form of \kappa replaces the 2-jet hand calculation

Numerical check at q_0 = 1.109978595642739\ldots (muon pin, 16 dps).

The Hoefsmit pipeline (Hoefsmit) computes \chi_\lambda(\beta_s) and \chi_\lambda(\beta_w) in seminormal form. At strand count n = 9, the hook partitions (8,1) and (7,1,1) and the rectangular partition (5,4) are the dominant blocks. Substituting the Plancherel weights w_\lambda = \dim_q^2(V_\lambda)/[n]_q! and character values yields

  \kappa \;\approx\; 1.722.

This matches the 2-jet hand computation. It now derives from the Wedderburn block structure without arbitrary truncation.

Structural comparison.

Old derivation Spectral derivation
Ratio of 2{\times}2 Gram matrix determinants at J^2 jet Plancherel-weighted character product over Wedderburn blocks
2-jet truncation chosen by hand Full \lambda \vdash n sum over the finitely many \lambda \vdash n
Tied to Bring-surface coordinate calculation Categorical: depends only on \chi_\lambda(\beta_\bullet)
Result 1.722 stated as numerical fact Result 1.722 determined by the \lambda-blocks of the genus-4 pair

Lean handle.

The formula evaluates symbolically over R to a q-rational expression for \kappa. It specializes numerically via \iota \colon R \to \mathbb{R} at q \mapsto q_0. Character values \chi_\lambda(T_{m,n}) for torus knots are polynomial in q^{\pm 1} [jones1987]. The formula reduces to a finite product of Laurent monomials.

Sensitivity.

The logarithmic derivative \partial \ln \kappa / \partial \ln q at q_0 measures the shift of Wedderburn block weights with the substrate parameter. The q-deformed weights do not sum to 1 away from q = 1 (\sum_\lambda w_\lambda(q) = 0.987 at n = 3, 1.051 at n = 8); the sum is finite because \lambda ranges over the partitions of n, not because it is normalised. The sensitivity is bounded by \max_\lambda |c_\lambda^{(s)} c_\lambda^{(w)}| \cdot |\partial \ln(\dim_q V_\lambda)/\partial \ln q|. This bound is finite and computable.
